docs.title: Survival Frontier Wiki
docs.text:
Survival Frontier is a co-op expansion custom game for Scrap Mechanic Survival. Drive your creations from afar, power your base with solar, cook your way up a tiered kitchen, fish the lakes and chemical pools, clear land with a Scythe, trade with a roaming merchant and take on shared side missions with your friends.

Get it on the Steam Workshop First steps

Current version // 1.4.1Fixes joining a friend's world when a lot of the map has been explored. 1.4.0 added the Traveling Trader, Pipe Couplers, Outpost Boards and a compact fishing HUD. See the Changelog.

docs.title: Systems
docs.text:
• Traveling Trader

    A roaming merchant who camps a few hundred metres to 1.5 km from the Hideout. Spend Frontier Scrip on machine blueprints, Backpack Expansions and his own dish recipes.

  • Contract Board

    Shared side missions for the whole party: Supply Runs, Courier, Pest Control, Survey Posts, Salvage and Catch Orders. Raise your Frontier Standing for better pay.

  • Frontier Kitchen

    35 new dishes in five tiers, researched at the Cookbot, with regeneration, damage resistance, deep breath and perk buffs.

  • Fishing

    Three rods, three baits and 12 fish across water, chemical pools and crude oil, including two legendaries. Plus junk and Sunken Crates.

  • Remote Control

    Drive your creations from outside with a handheld Remote, switch between Remote Cameras, send wireless signals and teleport between pads.

  • Power

    Solar Panels, Charge Controllers, Inverters, Mega Batteries, rechargeable batteries, Floodlights and Light Sensors.

  • Land Clearing

    The Scythe cuts bushes, shrubs, logs and more in an arc, and cleared land stays clear.

  • More

    Backpack Expansions · Scrapper · Pipe Coupler · Scannerbot · Gyro parts

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: What changed in each Survival Frontier update, newest first. The same notes are on the Workshop page's Change Notes tab.

• Fixed: joining a friend's world could fail with "Connection to host timed out" once a lot of the map had been explored. Land clearing kept a record for every explored area, and every record was sent to each player as they joined. In a big world that grew too large to send. The records now stay with the host, and joining players get a small summary instead, at most 192 entries for the whole map. The host's world converts itself the first time it loads with 1.4.1. There's nothing to do, and cleared land stays cleared.

• New: the Traveling Trader. He camps 300-1500 m from the Hideout and moves on every 2-3 days. Follow the map marker or type /trader. His Stall sells the Frontier machine blueprints (unlocked for the whole party), Backpack Expansions and 11 new trader-only dish recipes, all for Frontier Scrip. Spending scrip with him raises your reputation (Stranger, Customer, Regular, Partner), which opens the rarer stock. New worlds no longer start with the machine blueprints; existing worlds keep the ones they have.
  • New: the Pipe Coupler (trader blueprint). Two couplers dock when their flat faces touch, for example a lift platform set down against your base, and join the two vacuum pipe networks, so a Craftbot can use chests on the other side.
  • New: Outpost Boards (trader, Standing rank 3). Put one out in the world, 1.5 km from any other board, and new location contracts get posted around it as well as around the Hideout.
  • Contracts: the Contract Board is now the one at the Hideout (the craftable board is retired). A "New postings" button replaces every unaccepted offer for scrip; accepting no longer posts a free new offer. Abandoning puts the contract back and refunds anything handed in. Pest Control hunts are now at marked sites, Survey Posts need a real built structure (powered at higher tiers), every active location contract has a marker, and sites no longer land in lakes. Rewards and Standing ranks rebalanced; older saves keep their rank.
  • Fishing: a compact reeling panel just above the hotbar replaces the big bars over the crosshair, running fish splash instead of scraping, and in first person the line starts at the rod tip. The Carbon Rod is now a trader blueprint in new worlds.
  • Food: the Cookbot has a "Cookable now" tab that counts chests piped into it. Expedition and Feast dishes heal properly under the 100 HP cap, and recipes were rebalanced (fewer raid crops, Fish Chowder reworked).
  • Fixed: Floodlights now light up. Shots pass through bushes and plants again.

• New: the Scythe and land clearing. Craft a Scythe at the Craftbot (2 Wood + 2 Metal) and clear bushes, shrubs, saplings, ferns, reeds, burnt bushes, fallen logs and stumps, leaf and hay piles, fluff plants and coral. It cuts the plant you're aiming at and everything in a short arc in front of you. Cut plants don't grow back, and the Scythe never hurts creatures, players, builds or trees. This works in existing worlds too: plants become clearable the first time you go near them.
  • New: the Fishing Rod can also be crafted at the Craftbot, not just the Workbench.
  • Changed: crouch + Use on a Craftbot no longer opens the old Craft Queue window. Cancel crafts with the Cancel buttons under the Craftbot window.

• New: /bugreport also saves the reports you send to BugReports.json in your Survival Frontier folder, newest first, so you don't have to dig through the game log. This works whether you're hosting or joined someone else's game.

• Fixed: players joining a game could see the wrong version, missing items (Campfire, Contract Board, Frontier dishes), recipes that wouldn't craft, or raw names like obj_frontier_food_... after an update.
  • New: version check. When you join, chat shows your Survival Frontier version and the host's, and warns if they differ. Type /frontierversion to check any time.
  • Fixed: a HUD error with the food buff icons.

docs.title: Chat Commands
docs.text:
Survival Frontier adds these chat commands on top of the vanilla Survival ones. Type them in the chat box (press Enter to open chat).

Command What it does /trader Shows where the Traveling Trader is camped. /contracts Your Frontier Standing and the party's active contracts. /food Frontier Kitchen status: your cooking mastery, which dishes are researched, and your current food buffs. /fish Opens the Fish Journal: every species and the party's records. See Fishing. /frontierversion Shows your Survival Frontier version and the host's. See Multiplayer. /bugreport Opens a window to report a Survival Frontier bug. /bugreports Lists the bug reports saved in this world. The host can type /bugreports clear to empty the list. /scannerbot Shows whether the Scannerbot is on in this world. The host can type /scannerbot on or /scannerbot off.

Host-only options

Commands that change the world (/bugreports clear, /scannerbot on|off) only work for the host, because the host's game runs the world.

docs.title: First Steps
docs.text: Survival Frontier is a custom game: it replaces vanilla Survival with an expanded version, so you start a new world with it rather than adding it to an existing Survival save.

docs.title: Installing
docs.text:
1. Subscribe to Survival Frontier on the Steam Workshop.
  2. Start Scrap Mechanic, choose Play → Custom Games, and pick Survival Frontier.
  3. Create a new world. Friends who join need the same mod version (see Multiplayer).

docs.title: What you know from the start
docs.text:
A new Frontier world starts like vanilla Survival: crash site, Hideout and the vanilla progression. Three Frontier recipes are known from the start:

Item Where Why it matters early Campfire Workbench Cook simple Frontier meals before you can afford a Cookbot. See Frontier Kitchen. Fishing Rod Workbench or Craftbot Food from any lake, and fish for Catch Orders. See Fishing. Scythe Craftbot Clears bushes, logs and plants for good, so you can build. See Land Clearing.

The machine blueprints (solar power, the Remote Controller, Scrapper, Teleport Pads and so on) are not known in a new world. You buy them from the Traveling Trader with Frontier Scrip, which you earn from contracts.

docs.title: A suggested path
docs.text:
1. Survive the first days. Craft a Campfire and a Fishing Rod. Fish and Campfire dishes keep you fed while your farm gets going.
  2. Visit the Contract Board at the Hideout. Take a few low-tier contracts (Supply Runs and Catch Orders are easy early). They pay Frontier Scrip and raise your Frontier Standing.
  3. Find the Traveling Trader. Type /trader or follow his map marker. Your first scrip goes on Common blueprints. Every purchase raises the party's reputation with him, which opens the Uncommon, Rare and Legendary stock.
  4. Build up the kitchen. Once you have a Cookbot, cook dishes you know to research new ones. Higher tiers give regeneration, damage resistance and deep breath. See Frontier Kitchen.
  5. Go further out. Higher Standing brings longer, better-paying contracts: Survey Posts, big Salvage hauls and legendary Catch Orders. From rank 3 you can buy Outpost Boards to get contracts posted far from the Hideout.
  6. Late game. Remote Control for driving creations from outside, Teleport Pads, Mega Battery Banks and Backpack Expansions for up to 10 extra inventory rows.

Useful commands

/trader, /contracts, /food and /fish cover most questions in game. See Chat Commands.

docs.title: Multiplayer & Troubleshooting
docs.text: Survival Frontier is built for co-op. Most progress is shared by the whole party: trader blueprints, Frontier Standing and contracts. Each system's page says what is shared and what is per player.

docs.title: Everyone needs the same version
docs.text:
On someone else's server the host's copy of the mod runs the recipes and the game logic. If your version differs from the host's, you can see missing items, recipes that won't craft or odd item names.

  • When you join, chat shows your Survival Frontier version and the host's, and warns you if they differ.
  • Type /frontierversion to check any time.

docs.title: After an update: missing items or odd names
docs.text:
Symptoms: items missing from the crafting menus, names like obj_frontier_... instead of real names, or the game still on an old version after a Workshop update.

Scrap Mechanic keeps a cache of each mod and sometimes doesn't rebuild it after an update. To fix it:

  1. Close Scrap Mechanic.
  2. Delete the Cache folder in ...\Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\387990\3822729191\
  3. Start the game again. It rebuilds the cache automatically.

Tip

Close the game before Steam installs mod updates. Updating while the game is running is what usually leaves a stale cache behind.

docs.title: "Connection to host timed out" when joining
docs.text:
Symptoms: the host can join your game, but joining theirs loads for about a minute and then fails with "Connection to host timed out. Please check your Internet connection and try again."

With Survival Frontier 1.4.0 this happened in worlds where a lot of the map had been explored, because of how land clearing saved its progress. 1.4.1 fixes it.

  1. Everyone updates to 1.4.1. Check with /frontierversion.
  2. The host loads their world once. It converts itself within a few seconds of loading.
  3. Join again.

If it still times out, check the usual network causes on the host's PC: the game allowed through Windows Firewall on both Private and Public networks, no third-party firewall or VPN blocking it. Then send a /bugreport.

docs.title: Reporting bugs
docs.text:
Type /bugreport in game. A window opens where you describe what happened. The report is:

  • saved with the host's world (the host can list them with /bugreports),
  • written to the game log, and
  • saved to BugReports.json in your own Survival Frontier folder (...\Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\387990\3822729191\), newest first. This works whether you're hosting or joined someone else's game.

You can also leave feedback in the comments on the Workshop page.

docs.text:
Permanently adds one row (10 slots) to your inventory. Hold it and keep Create held for 5 seconds to use - let go early to cancel.Up to 10 extra rows per player. Rare - found far from home or bought from traders.

docs.title: Pipe Coupler
docs.text:

docs.title: Backpack Expansions
docs.text:
A Backpack Expansion permanently adds one row of 10 slots to your inventory. Each player can use up to 10, for 100 extra slots in all. Backpack Expansions can't be crafted. You find them in loot far from the crash site, pull them up in Sunken Crates while fishing far out, win them from top-tier contracts, or buy them from the Traveling Trader once he trusts you.

At a glance

  • +1 row (10 slots) per expansion, up to +10 rows per player.
  • Per player: the extra rows are yours alone, saved with the world, and still there when you rejoin.
  • To use: hold it and keep Create (left-click) held for 5 seconds.
  • Where to get one: ruin chests and epic or legendary loot crates far from the crash site, far-out Sunken Crates, tier 5 contracts, and the Traveling Trader (800 scrip, Partner reputation).
  • No recipe. They stack up to 10.

docs.title: How to use one
docs.text:
1. Put the Backpack Expansion in your hotbar and select it.
  2. Hold Create (left-click). A progress circle fills over 5 seconds.
  3. When it's full, one expansion is used up and your inventory grows by one row. A message shows your new total, for example "Backpack expanded! +3 rows (3/10)".

Let go before the circle fills and nothing happens, so you can't use one by accident.

Once you have all 10 rows, you get "Your backpack is already at the maximum (+10 rows)" and the expansion isn't used up. Give the spare to a friend.

docs.title: Per player, and permanent
docs.text:
• The rows belong to the player who used the expansion, not to the world or the party.
  • They're saved with the world. Leave and rejoin and your inventory is still the bigger size.
  • In someone else's world, your rows are saved in that world. They don't follow you to other saves.
Expansions used Extra slots 1 +10 5 +50 10 (maximum) +100

docs.title: Loot far from the crash site
docs.text:
Backpack Expansions can turn up in ruin chests and in epic and legendary loot crates, but only far from the start:

Distance from the crash site Chance Under 600 m none 600 m to 2,500 m rises steadily with distance 2,500 m and more full chance

At full chance, that's about:

Container Chance of a Backpack Expansion Ruin chest about 1% Epic loot crate about 3% Legendary loot crate about 10%

It's the farthest player who counts

The game can't tell where a chest is, so it goes by the farthest player's distance from the crash site at the moment the chest fills. Containers fill as areas load around players, so explore far out yourself to get the full chance.

docs.title: Sunken Crates (fishing)
docs.text: When fishing, some casts bring up a Sunken Crate instead of a fish. In the far band (2,500 m and more from the crash site) a Sunken Crate also has a 5% chance to hold a Backpack Expansion, on top of its usual loot. Crates from the near and mid bands never have one.

docs.title: Contracts
docs.text:
Only tier 5 contracts can pay a Backpack Expansion. The chance is rolled once, when the contract is done, so you can't see it on the board beforehand:

Contract Chance at tier 5 Supply Run none Courier 3% Pest Control 8% Survey Post 8% Catch Order 8% Salvage 15%

When you're lucky, the completion message says "- with a Backpack Expansion!", and it's part of the reward you claim at the board.

docs.title: Traveling Trader
docs.text:
The Traveling Trader sells Backpack Expansions on his Gear tab:

Price Needs 800 Frontier Scrip Partner reputation (the party has spent 600 scrip with him in total)

The expansion stays on show, locked, until you reach Partner.

Tip

Expansions are items, so whoever finds or buys one can hand it to anyone in the party.

docs.title: Land Clearing & the Scythe
docs.text:
The Scythe is a hand tool for clearing bushes, reeds and undergrowth off the land, to make room for bases, roads and farms. One swing cuts every clearable plant in an arc in front of you. Cut plants never grow back. It works in new worlds and in worlds you started before the update. The Scythe can't hurt creatures, players, builds, trees or stones.

At a glance

  • Recipe: Craftbot, 2 Wood Block + 2 Metal Block, 20 s. Known from the start: no blueprint needed.
  • Reach: 2.5 m, measured to the plant's edge, and 60° either side of where you're facing (a 120° arc).
  • Up to 40 plants per swing. Hold left-click to keep swinging.
  • Cut plants are gone for good, and the save remembers it.
  • Works in existing worlds: plants become clearable the first time you go near them.
  • Multiplayer: anyone can clear, and everyone sees the result.

docs.title: Getting a Scythe
docs.text:
Crafted at Ingredients Time Makes Craftbot 2 × Wood Block, 2 × Metal Block 20 s 1 Scythe

Every world knows this recipe from the start. You don't need a Traveling Trader blueprint for it. See Recipes for the full list.

docs.title: Using it
docs.text:
1. Put the Scythe in your hotbar and select it.
  2. Look at a plant. If the Scythe can cut it, you'll see [LMB] Cut.
  3. Left-click to swing. Hold left-click to keep swinging, at the same pace as the sledgehammer.

At the moment the blade would hit, every clearable plant in the arc is cut down with a burst of leaves (or ash, for burnt plants).

docs.title: What counts as "in front of you"
docs.text:
Rule Value Reach 2.5 m from you to the edge of the plant (big bushes count as soon as their edge is in reach) Arc 60° either side of the way you're facing Height from 1.6 m below your feet to 2.5 m above them Plants per swing 40 at most, nearest first Swing rate about one every 0.6 s, like the sledgehammer

Plants that are very close to you (within half a metre) are cut wherever they are, even if they're beside you.

Aim at big bushes

The plant under your crosshair is always cut, even if it's a bit outside the arc. It counts if the point you're aiming at is no more than about 4.5 m away. This helps with large bushes whose middle is out of reach but whose leaves aren't.

docs.title: Terrain plants
docs.text:
Cutting these gives you nothing. They're only there to be cleared.

Kind Includes Cut effect Bushes wild bushes, column shrubs, buxus, boxwood burst of leaves Burnt-forest plants burnt bushes and small burnt bushes, burnt ferns, burnt perennials, burnt thorns ash Small plants exotic plants, pad plants, ferns, perennials, green sprouts, small birch saplings, fan sprouts, cave fluff patches burst of leaves Decorative farm plants the corn, cucumber and eggplant plants built into farm areas burst of leaves Waterside plants reeds, sea plants, sunflowers burst of leaves Burnt wood fallen burnt logs, burnt stumps ash

You can cut reeds and sea plants from the shore or while wading.

docs.title: Vanilla vegetation
docs.text:
These are broken through their own normal behaviour, so they act exactly as if you'd hit them some other way:

Plant Drops Leaf piles nothing Hay piles nothing Fluff plants nothing Bacterius nothing Coral its usual loot

docs.title: What's never affected
docs.text:
• Trees of any kind (chop them with the sledgehammer as usual), including the Giant Tree.
  • Crops you pick, such as corn, cotton and pigment flowers, and anything you've planted.
  • Ground grass. It's part of the terrain, not an object, so nothing can cut it.
  • Stones, dirt patches, creatures, players, your builds and vehicles. The Scythe never makes a melee attack, so it can't damage anything.

Only the Scythe clears

Sledgehammers, explosions, weapons and vehicles leave terrain plants alone, as they always did.

Players still walk through bushes, reeds and ferns, and shots fly through them. Fallen logs and stumps stay solid until you cut them.

docs.title: Cut plants never come back
docs.text: Clearing is permanent. A cut plant is saved as gone with the world, and it doesn't grow back after a reload, a new day or anything else. Cleared land stays clear for your base.

docs.title: Existing worlds
docs.text:
You don't need a new world. Each area's plants become clearable the first time that area loads near a player after the update. Until then they look and behave exactly as before.

  • Plants stay in the same places, with the same shape, size and colour.
  • In a dense area the change happens over the first few moments without a hitch, so a plant you swing at right away may not be cuttable yet. Swing again a moment later.
  • If an area can't be converted for any reason, its plants just stay as normal scenery. You can't lose plants because of it.

Only the overworld is affected. Interiors and other worlds keep their plants as they are.

docs.title: Multiplayer
docs.text:
• Anyone with a Scythe can clear, host or not.
  • Cutting is done on the host, so every player sees the same cleared land, and it's saved with the host's world.
  • Joining players only receive a small summary of which areas are converted, so a well-explored world stays quick to join. (In 1.4.0 a big world could stop friends joining; 1.4.1 fixes that. See Multiplayer.)
  • Everyone should have the same Survival Frontier version. See Multiplayer.

docs.title: Contract Board
docs.text:
The Contract Board is where the whole party picks up side missions out on the frontier: supply runs, courier jobs, pest control, survey posts, salvage hauls and catch orders. Every contract you finish pays Frontier Scrip plus materials (and often food), and raises the party's Frontier Standing. Higher Standing brings harder contracts, farther from home, that pay more. The first board stands at the Hideout. Later you can buy Outpost Boards from the Traveling Trader to post contracts deeper in the wilderness.

At a glance

  • Where: the Contract Board stands next to the trader at the Hideout. It's placed there automatically and can't be crafted.
  • 4 offers and up to 3 active contracts, shared by the whole party.
  • New offers every 20 minutes, or right away with New postings for 2 × your rank in scrip.
  • 6 contract types: Supply Run, Courier, Pest Control, Survey Post, Salvage, Catch Order.
  • Frontier Standing goes from rank 1 to rank 5. You need 5 / 15 / 35 / 70 finished contracts for ranks 2-5.
  • Rewards: 3-94 Frontier Scrip, a material bundle, a 50% chance of Frontier dishes. Tier 5 contracts also have a hidden chance of a Backpack Expansion.
  • Outpost Boards (rank 3, from the Traveling Trader) post contracts around themselves once they stand at least 1.5 km from every other board.
  • Active contracts show up in the Logbook, the quest tracker and the compass.

docs.title: The board window
docs.text:
Press Use on a board to open the Frontier Contracts window.

  • Top line: your Frontier Standing, how many contracts the party has finished, and how many more you need for the next rank.
  • Available (left): up to 4 offers. Each card shows the contract, its tier, where it is (for example "about 1.9 km north-east of Outpost 2"), and the reward. Click Accept to take one.
  • Active (right): up to 3 contracts the party is working on, each with a progress line and its reward. The main button changes with what the contract needs:
    • Hand in for Supply Runs and Catch Orders
    • New parcel / New beacon to get a replacement for a lost Sealed Parcel or Survey Beacon
    • Claim once the contract is done
  • Abandon gives up an active contract.
  • Footer: time left until the next refresh. On an Outpost Board it also says whether that outpost is open, and if not, why.

Every board shows the same contracts. Hand-ins, claims and replacement items work at any Contract Board, the Hideout's or an outpost's. Salvage is the one exception (see Salvage).

docs.title: Offers, refreshes and new postings
docs.text:
• The board always tries to keep 4 offers, and avoids repeating a contract type, so the 4 offers are usually 4 different types.
  • Accepting an offer does not put a new one in its place. A new offer appears when a contract is claimed, at the next refresh, or when someone buys new postings.
  • Every 20 minutes all offers nobody has accepted are replaced. Everyone gets a chat line. Players within 200 m of the Hideout board also get an on-screen alert, but only while the party has a free active slot.
  • New postings replaces every unaccepted offer right away. It costs 2 × your Standing rank in Frontier Scrip (2 at rank 1, 10 at rank 5), paid by whoever clicks. It doesn't reset the 20-minute timer.
Rank New postings cost 1 2 scrip 2 4 scrip 3 6 scrip 4 8 scrip 5 10 scrip

docs.title: Accepting, abandoning and claiming
docs.text:
• You can only accept while the party has fewer than 3 active contracts.
  • Courier and Survey Post contracts give the player who accepts the item they need (a Sealed Parcel or a Survey Beacon). If that player's inventory is full, the contract can't be accepted.
  • Abandoning puts the contract back on the board exactly as it was offered: same site, same reward. It only goes back if there's a free offer slot (fewer than 4 offers). Its progress is reset, and any Salvage Crate already out in the world disappears.
  • If items were already handed in, Abandon asks first: the button turns into Confirm for a few seconds, and the handed-in items go back to the player who abandons. That player needs room for them.
  • Claiming gives the whole reward to the player who clicks Claim. If that player doesn't have room, nothing is lost. Make space and claim again.

Refunds on \"any\" orders

On an "(any)" order, such as Lake Fish (any) or Campfire dishes (any), abandoning gives back the same number of items, but all as one kind from the list. That kind may not be what you handed in.

No rerolling by clicking

Accepting and then abandoning leaves the board exactly as it was. Rewards are set when the offer is posted. To see different offers, pay for New postings or wait for the refresh.

docs.title: Contract tiers and distances
docs.text:
Each contract has a tier from 1 to 5. Offers are posted at your Standing rank or one below it:

Standing rank Tiers offered 1 1 2 1-2 3 2-3 4 3-4 5 4-5

Contracts with a location (Courier, Pest Control, Survey Post, Salvage) send you a set distance from a board. The distance depends on the tier:

Tier Distance from the board 1 250-500 m 2 400-800 m 3 700-1,300 m 4 1,100-1,900 m 5 1,600-2,600 m

Each site is picked when the offer is posted, around the Hideout board or a random open Outpost Board. The card tells you the distance, the compass direction and which board it's measured from. Sites stay inside the world, avoid lakes, and are never closer to the start area than the board is, so contracts don't send you back toward spawn.

There are no time limits: an active contract stays until you finish it or abandon it.

docs.title: Supply Run
docs.text:
Hand in items at any board. Partial hand-ins count: each Hand in click takes as many matching items from your inventory as the contract still needs. Each offer asks for one of these:

Tier Possible asks 1 6 Cotton · 60 Metal Blocks · 62 Potatoes · 12 Corn · 3 Campfire dishes (any) 2 7 Component Kits · 4 Glue · 20 Cotton · 50 Chemicals · 3 Homestead dishes (any) 3 26 Batteries · 37 Gas Canisters · 4 Circuit Boards · 11 Beeswax · 2 Expedition dishes (any) 4 11 Circuit Boards · 6 Crystals · 11 Glowpoop · 3 Frontier Feast dishes (any) 5 16 Circuit Boards · 10 Crystals · 16 Glowpoop · 4 Frontier Feast dishes (any)

Dish asks take any dish of that cooking tier. See the Frontier Kitchen.

docs.title: Courier (Sealed Parcel)
docs.text: You get a Sealed Parcel when you accept. Carry it to the marked spot. The delivery happens by itself when any party member with a parcel in their inventory gets within 20 m of the spot. Lost the parcel? Any board's New parcel button gives you another.

docs.title: Pest Control
docs.text:
A pack of robots is causing trouble at a marked site. Destroy the required number within 150 m of the site. The pack spawns when someone in the party first gets within 150 m. Wild robots of the same kind that happen to be near the site count too.

Tier Target (one is picked) 1 4 Totebots 2 3 Haybots 3 3 Tapebots 4 2 Farmbots, or 3 Tapebots 5 3 Farmbots, or 7 Tapebots
  • Robots that die in water (drowned, swimming or diving) don't count.
  • Raiders attacking your farm don't count.
  • One kill counts for one contract only. If two active hunts want the same robot, the older contract gets it.
  • If the site turns out to be under water, the pack is moved to the nearest dry ground. If there's none nearby, the site is moved and marked somewhere drier.

docs.title: Survey Post (Survey Beacon)
docs.text:
You get a Survey Beacon when you accept. Set it up within 25 m of the marked site and keep it up for 10 seconds. From tier 2 it has to sit high up on a structure you build there:

Tier Beacon height above the ground Structure size Power needed 1 on the ground none no 2 2 m 8 parts no 3 4 m 18 parts no 4 7 m 35 parts yes 5 10 m 60 parts yes
  • Height is measured from the beacon's base down to the terrain directly below it.
  • Parts are counted per placed part. One dragged run of blocks counts as one part, so build with separate pieces.
  • The structure must be static (built in place). A beacon on a vehicle doesn't count, even a parked one.
  • Power (tiers 4-5): the structure must include a Battery Container, Solar Panel, Mega Battery or Mega Battery Bank.
  • The progress line tells you what's still missing (for example "Beacon 3.2 / 7 m up, structure 20 / 35 parts - needs a battery or solar panel on it") and counts the 10 seconds once everything is right. If the post stops meeting the requirements, the count starts over.
  • You can pick the beacon back up at any time. Lost it? Any board's New beacon button gives you another.

docs.title: Salvage
docs.text:
A Salvage Crate waits at the marked spot. It appears once someone in the party gets within 150 m. Haul it to within 20 m of the board the contract names. It's handed in by itself when it gets there.

Crates are too heavy to carry by hand, nothing can be built onto them, and they can't be picked up with the hammer. You need a vehicle that can pick a crate up and carry it: a flatbed, crane or loader. Bigger crates pay more:

Crate Size (blocks) Pay Tier 1 Tier 2 Tier 3 Tier 4 Tier 5 Small Salvage Crate 2×2×2 ×1.0 60% 20% – – – Salvage Crate 3×3×3 ×1.25 40% 60% 30% – – Large Salvage Crate 5×5×5 ×1.6 – 20% 60% 50% – Huge Salvage Crate 8×8×8 ×2.2 – – 10% 50% 60% Colossal Salvage Crate 12×12×12 ×2.5 – – – – 40%

The crate size is shown on the offer before you accept.

  • Where to deliver: a contract posted from an Outpost Board goes back to that Outpost Board, as long as it's still open and hasn't been moved more than 20 m. Otherwise (and for everything posted from the Hideout) it goes to the Hideout board.
  • The quest marker follows the crate once it's found.
  • If the crate is destroyed, a new one waits back at the site.
  • If the site is under water, the crate is placed on the nearest dry ground within 96 m. If there isn't any, the site moves about 250 m and is marked again.

Hauling big crates

  • Look at the crate size before you accept. A 2-block crate fits on a small cart, but a Huge (8 blocks) or Colossal (12 blocks) crate needs a real hauler: a wide flatbed with a crane or a lifter.
  • Bring the vehicle with you. The crate only spawns once someone is within 150 m of the site, and you can't build onto it to make it drivable.
  • An open Outpost Board near the site gives salvage from its contracts a much shorter trip home.

docs.title: Catch Order
docs.text:
Catch fish and hand them in at any board, like a Supply Run (partial hand-ins count). See Fishing. In game, /fish shows where each fish lives.

Tier Possible orders 1 6 Lake Fish (any of Pond Perch, Mud Carp, Moonfin, Sunscale Trout) · 4 Glowgills · 4 Slick Minnows 2 3 Moonfins · 3 Sunscale Trout · 6 Mud Carp · 6 Glowgills 3 1 Ironjaw Pike · 2 Sludge Eels · 2 Tarback Catfish 4 2 Ironjaw Pike · 1 Three-Eyed Tetra · 2 Tarback Catfish 5 2 Three-Eyed Tetras · 3 Big Fish (any of Ironjaw Pike, Sludge Eel, Tarback Catfish) · 1 Frontier Sturgeon* · 1 Crude Leviathan*

* Legendary orders are only offered once the party has a Frontier Rod, because these fish can't be landed without one. Orders for fish that need a Carbon Rod say so in their title.

Catch Orders pay bait on top of the usual reward:

Tier Bait 1 8 Basic Bait 2 6 Glow Bait 3 8 Glow Bait 4 4 Prime Bait 5 6 Prime Bait

The Frontier Rod

Catch Orders of tier 3 and up include a Frontier Rod in their reward until someone in the party claims one. The Frontier Rod has no recipe, so this is the only way to get it. After the first one is claimed, new orders stop paying it.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
Every contract pays three things:

  1. Frontier Scrip. The amount depends on the tier and the contract type:

    Type Tier 1 Tier 2 Tier 3 Tier 4 Tier 5 Supply Run 3 6 10 16 25 Courier 4 7 12 19 30 Survey Post 4 8 13 21 33 Catch Order 4 8 13 21 33 Pest Control 5 10 16 26 40 Salvage (Small crate) 5 9 15 24 38 Salvage (Salvage Crate) 6 11 19 30 47 Salvage (Large) 7 14 24 38 60 Salvage (Huge) 10 20 33 53 83 Salvage (Colossal) 11 23 38 60 94

    Not every crate size appears at every tier (see the crate table). Spend scrip at the Traveling Trader.

  2. A material bundle, picked at random from the contract's tier:

    Tier Base bundle (one of) 1 30 Wood Blocks · 20 Metal Blocks · 1 Component Kit 2 3 Component Kits · 4 Glue · 2 Batteries 3 3 Circuit Boards · 5 Batteries · 10 Gas Canisters 4 4 Circuit Boards · 5 Component Kits · 8 Batteries 5 6 Circuit Boards · 8 Component Kits · 7 Crystals

    The base amount grows with better-paying contracts, but more slowly than the scrip does: about ×1.1 for Courier, Survey Post and Catch Order, ×1.27 for Pest Control, and from ×1.22 (Small crate) up to ×1.94 (Colossal crate) for Salvage. Supply Runs pay the base amount.

  3. A 50% chance of Frontier dishes: 2 dishes, or 3 on tier 4-5 contracts. They come from the highest cooking tier the party has researched (capped at the contract's tier), and the party's researched dishes are preferred. If the party hasn't researched any dishes yet, they're Campfire dishes. Traveling Trader dishes are never paid out.

Catch Orders also pay bait and possibly the Frontier Rod (see Catch Order).

The full reward is listed on the card before you accept and doesn't change afterwards. The one exception is the Backpack Expansion.

docs.title: Backpack Expansion (tier 5)
docs.text:
On tier 5 contracts there's a chance the reward also includes a Backpack Expansion. The board shows the chance on the card. The roll happens once, when the contract is finished, so it can't be seen in advance or rerolled:

Type Chance (tier 5 only) Supply Run 0% Courier 3% Pest Control 8% Survey Post 8% Catch Order 8% Salvage 15%

If it hits, the "Contract done" message says so, and the expansion is added to the reward you claim.

docs.title: Frontier Standing
docs.text:
Every finished contract adds one to the party's count. Standing is shared by the whole party.

Rank Contracts finished What it brings 1 0 Tier 1 contracts 2 5 Tier 1-2 contracts 3 15 Tier 2-3 contracts. Tier 3 Catch Orders (the Frontier Rod). Outpost Boards can be bought from the Traveling Trader. 4 35 Tier 3-4 contracts. Powered Survey Posts. 5 70 Tier 4-5 contracts. The Backpack Expansion chance. Legendary Catch Orders (with a Frontier Rod). New postings cost 10 scrip.

When the party ranks up, everyone gets an alert. Type /contracts in chat to see your rank, how many contracts you've finished and every active contract with its progress. See Commands.

docs.title: Outpost Boards
docs.text:
An Outpost Board lets the party take contracts deeper into the frontier.

  • How to get one: buy it from the Traveling Trader for Frontier Scrip once the party reaches Frontier Standing rank 3. The first one costs 400 scrip, and each one after that costs 200 more (400, 600, 800 …). The party can buy at most 6.
  • Placement rule: an Outpost Board only opens if it is:
    • built in place on solid ground, not on a vehicle
    • out in the open world
    • at least 1.5 km (measured flat on the map) from the Hideout board and from every Outpost Board that was already open
  • Open boards are numbered in order (Outpost 1, Outpost 2 …). If one isn't open, its window's footer tells you why, for example "it's only 0.9 km from the board at the Hideout - it needs 1.5 km". When a board opens, everyone gets an alert.
  • What it does: once it's open, new location contracts are posted around it as well as around the Hideout. Each new site is centred on one of the open boards, picked at random. Salvage from those contracts is delivered to that Outpost Board. Like any board, it also takes hand-ins, claims and replacement parcels and beacons.
  • Moving it: pick it back up with the hammer and set it up somewhere else. You can't lift it onto a vehicle or build onto it. If an outpost is removed, a closed one nearby may open in its place.

Where to put an outpost

Put Outpost Boards near the far areas you want to work. Contracts posted from an outpost measure their distance from it, so your trips start out there and not at the Hideout. Salvage crates from those contracts only need to reach that outpost.

docs.title: Logbook, compass and markers
docs.text:
• Every active contract appears as a side quest in the vanilla Logbook and quest tracker. The title and progress update as you go.
  • Every active contract with a location gets a quest marker in the world and on the compass. For Salvage, the marker moves to the crate once it's found. The contract you track in the Logbook has a bright marker and the others are dimmed, so you can follow every contract without switching the tracked one.
  • Finished, claimed and abandoned contracts leave the Logbook by themselves.

docs.title: Playing with a party
docs.text:
• Contracts, offers and Standing belong to the whole party. Everyone sees the same board, and anyone can accept, hand in, abandon or claim.
  • Anyone's progress counts. Any player can deliver a parcel, kill the robots, set up the beacon or haul the crate.
  • Hand-ins come from the inventory of the player who clicks.
  • Items given on accept (parcel, beacon) and the reward on claim go to the player who clicks. Share them out yourselves.
  • New postings are paid by whoever clicks the button.

docs.title: Fishing
docs.text:
Cast a rod into a lake, a chemical pool or a pool of crude oil, wait for the bobber to dip, hook the bite and reel it in. There are 12 fish to find, including two legendaries. Which ones bite depends on the kind of water, how far you are from the crash site, the time of day, your rod and your bait. Big fish fight back on the line. Every so often you pull up junk or a Sunken Crate full of loot instead. Fish are filleted into Fish Fillets for the Frontier Kitchen, they can be handed in for Catch Orders, and the party's best catches go into the Fish Journal.

At a glance

  • Rods: Fishing Rod (Workbench or Craftbot, known from the start), Carbon Rod (Craftbot, Traveling Trader blueprint), Frontier Rod (Catch Order reward only).
  • Water: lakes and ponds, chemical pools, crude oil. Each kind has its own fish and junk.
  • Distance bands from the crash site: near (under 600 m), mid (600-2,500 m), far (2,500 m and more).
  • Time windows: day, night, and dawn/dusk.
  • Bait: bites come 30-40% sooner. Glow Bait draws the night and chemical fish. The legendaries take nothing but Prime Bait.
  • Other catches: a Sunken Crate on 2 / 4 / 6% of casts (near / mid / far), and junk on 12% of the rest.
  • Fish Journal: type /fish in chat.

docs.title: Rods
docs.text:
Rod How to get it Hook window Sweet spot Tension climb Fishing Rod (tier 1) Workbench or Craftbot. Known from the start. 1.2 s 34% wide (38-72%) 0.55 per second Carbon Rod (tier 2) Craftbot, once the party owns the Carbon Rod blueprint from the Traveling Trader 1.6 s 44% wide (33-77%) 0.42 per second Frontier Rod (tier 3) Can't be crafted. Paid out by tier 3 and higher Catch Orders. 2.0 s 52% wide (29-81%) 0.34 per second

What the stats mean:

  • Hook window: how long you have to click after a bite before the fish gets away.
  • Sweet spot: the band on the line-tension bar where reeling works best. It is always centred on 55% tension, and a better rod widens it.
  • Tension climb: how fast the line tightens while you hold the reel. The fish scales it: a hard-fighting fish tightens the line faster. A lower number gives you more time before the line snaps.

A better rod also brings bites a little sooner: the wait is 10% shorter with the Carbon Rod and 20% shorter with the Frontier Rod.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
Rod Where Ingredients Craft time Fishing Rod Workbench or Craftbot 8 Scrap Wood Block, 2 Scrap Metal Block, 2 Cotton 30 s Carbon Rod Craftbot (needs the blueprint) 6 Metal Block Level 2, 2 Component Kit, 4 Cotton, 1 Circuit Board 60 s

The Carbon Rod is an Uncommon blueprint. The trader sells it for 72 Frontier Scrip once the party reaches the trader's second reputation level (60 scrip spent in total). A blueprint unlocks the recipe for the whole party. See Traveling Trader.

The Frontier Rod has no recipe. Catch Orders of tier 3 and higher pay one, until someone in the party claims it. After that, new Catch Orders stop paying it. See Catch Orders.

docs.title: Which fish a rod can land
docs.text: Every fish has a minimum rod: tier 1 (any rod), tier 2 (Carbon Rod or better) or tier 3 (Frontier Rod). A fish that needs a better rod than yours can still bite, but 70% less often than it otherwise would. When you hook it, the line snaps straight away: "Something huge snapped your line! You need a stronger rod." Your bait is used up.

docs.title: How to fish
docs.text:
Default controls: Create (left mouse button) does everything.

  1. Cast. Hold the rod in your hotbar, then hold Create to wind up. A full wind-up takes 2.2 s, and a longer wind-up throws further: from 6 m up to 20 m. While you wind up, a preview bobber floats where the cast will land, and the action line shows the distance and the kind of water (for example 14 m - chemical). It shows No water there if the spot is dry. Let go to throw.
  2. Wait. The bobber has to land in water. If it lands on dry ground you get "No water there - cast into a lake, pond or pool" and nothing happens. A bite comes after 5-25 seconds (shorter with bait and a better rod, see below). If a fish is on its way, its shadow circles the bobber and closes in as the bite gets near. No shadow means junk or a Sunken Crate.
  3. Tease (optional). While you wait, each fresh click of Create cuts the time left before a bite to 75%, up to 4 times. Holding Create reels the bobber in at 1.5 m/s. If you reel it to within 3 m of you, or onto the shore, the cast ends.
  4. Hook the bite. The bobber splashes and you get "Bite! Click to hook it!". Click Create within your rod's hook window (1.2 / 1.6 / 2.0 s). If you are too slow, it gets away. A missed bite doesn't use bait.
  5. Reel it in. Everything you hook fights, even small fish and junk. See The reeling fight.

The cast is called off if you put the rod away or walk more than 32 m from your bobber.

docs.title: Bite wait times
docs.text:
The wait is a random 5-25 seconds. Bait and the rod tier multiply it:

No bait Basic / Glow Bait (x0.7) Prime Bait (x0.6) Fishing Rod 5-25 s 3.5-17.5 s 3-15 s Carbon Rod (x0.9) 4.5-22.5 s 3.2-15.8 s 2.7-13.5 s Frontier Rod (x0.8) 4-20 s 2.8-14 s 2.4-12 s

Teasing shortens these further.

docs.title: The reeling fight
docs.text:
Once a fish is hooked, a compact reeling panel appears just above your hotbar. Your movement is slowed while you fight. The panel has three bars:

Bar Shows Colours LINE Line tension, with your rod's sweet spot shaded yellow when slack, green in the sweet spot, orange above it, red at 90% and up FISH The fish's strength (stamina) orange, turning green once it's tired (below 25%) or exhausted. Reads JUNK or HEAVY when you've snagged junk or a crate. REEL How far it's been reeled in fills up; full means it's landed

Under the panel, the action line tells you what to do: Hold to reel, It's about to run - stop reeling!, Let go - it's running!, Line's too tight - let go!, Slack line - hold to reel, It's exhausted - hold to reel it in.

How it works:

  • Hold Create to reel. Reeling pulls the fish in and raises the tension. Letting go drops the tension by 50% of the bar per second. Every fight starts at 35% tension with the fish 8% of the way in.
  • Keep the tension at or above the sweet spot to tire the fish. That drains the fish's stamina, and a tired fish comes in faster: a fresh fish gives only 30% of the normal reel speed, an exhausted one gives all of it. Reeling while the tension is inside the sweet spot pulls in 1.8 times faster. With the line slack (below the sweet spot), the fish gets its breath back.
  • Runs. Every so often the fish makes a run. First it thrashes and splashes for 0.6 s ("It's about to run - stop reeling!"), then it pulls. Let go during a run. The drag gives it line and holds the tension steady, at 50% plus up to 30% more for the hardest fighters. If you reel against a run, the tension spikes fast. Either way you lose some ground during a run, and it jolts the camera and drags you towards the water. Runs come at least 1.5 s apart, and a fresh, strong fish runs more often and for longer.
  • Tugs. Between runs the fish jerks the line now and then, which kicks the tension up a little.
  • Exhausted. When its stamina is nearly gone (2%), the fish stops running and tugging. The tension can't climb past the top of the sweet spot, and it comes in 1.5 times faster. Let the line go slack for too long and it recovers: once it's back to 15% stamina, it fights again.

How a fight ends:

Result When Landed The REEL bar fills. The catch goes into your inventory, or drops at your feet if your inventory is full. The line snapped! Tension stays at the very top for 0.3 s. It got away... The line stays slack (5% tension or less) for 2.5 s.

Watch the line

Holding the reel down the whole time doesn't win. The tension keeps climbing until the line snaps, much faster against a run. Reel between runs, ease off when the bar turns orange or red, and let go the moment the fish runs.

How hard each catch pulls: small fish pull lightly (strength 0.2), and junk and crates are dead weight (0.1, with no runs and no stamina). The big fish each have their own strength, from 0.45 (Tarback Catfish) up to 0.9 (Crude Leviathan), shown in the fish table. A Sunken Crate is very heavy: its tension climbs 1.6 times faster and it comes in at 55% of the normal speed. Feather the reel.

Note

Land your catch within 2 minutes of the bite. After that the catch is no longer accepted.

docs.title: Water types
docs.text:
When you cast, the game checks the spot straight down from where the bobber will land. It has to be one of the world's water areas, and the kind of water decides which fish and junk you can catch there:

Water Where Fish Water Lakes and ponds Pond Perch, Mud Carp, Moonfin, Sunscale Trout, Ironjaw Pike, Frontier Sturgeon Chemical Chemical pools Glowgill, Sludge Eel, Three-Eyed Tetra Crude oil Oil pools Slick Minnow, Tarback Catfish, Crude Leviathan

The splashes and the sounds of a running fish match the water you're in.

docs.title: Distance from the crash site
docs.text:
The distance is measured flat across the map, from the crash site (the start area) to your bobber.

Band Distance Near under 600 m Mid 600 m to 2,500 m Far 2,500 m and more

A fish's band is the closest band it lives in. It also bites in every band further out. A Pond Perch bites anywhere, a Sunscale Trout bites in the mid and far bands, and an Ironjaw Pike only in the far band. The band also sets the Sunken Crate chance (see Junk and Sunken Crates).

docs.title: Time of day
docs.text:
Window In-game clock (about) Night 21:00 to 05:00 Dawn 05:00 to 07:12 Day 07:12 to 18:00 Dusk 18:00 to 21:00

Fish marked any bite at all hours. Moonfin, Sludge Eel and Crude Leviathan bite only at night. Sunscale Trout bites only by day. Frontier Sturgeon bites only at dawn and dusk.

docs.title: Bait
docs.text:
Bait stays in your inventory. You don't hold it. Each cast uses the most useful bait you're carrying for that spot:

  1. Glow Bait if a fish that loves it can bite here, or Prime Bait if a legendary can bite here and you're holding a Frontier Rod.
  2. Otherwise Basic Bait.
  3. Otherwise whatever bait you have.

One bait is used each time you land something (fish, junk or crate) or the line snaps. A missed bite or a fish that gets away costs nothing.

Bait Recipe (Workbench) Bite wait Special Basic Bait 1 Carrot + 1 Corn → 4 (10 s) x0.7 (30% sooner) none Glow Bait 1 Glowgill + 1 Corn → 4 (10 s) x0.7 (30% sooner) Moonfin bites 2.5x, Sludge Eel 2x and Three-Eyed Tetra 3x as often Prime Bait 3 Fish Fillet + 1 Chili Pepper → 2 (15 s) x0.6 (40% sooner) Required for the Frontier Sturgeon and Crude Leviathan

All three bait recipes are known from the start. Catch Orders also pay bait (see below).

Legendaries need both

The Frontier Sturgeon and Crude Leviathan never bite without Prime Bait. With Prime Bait but a weaker rod they can bite, but they snap the line every time. Bring a Frontier Rod and Prime Bait.

docs.title: The 12 fish
docs.text:
Commonness is how often a fish bites compared with the other fish that can bite in the same spot. For example, in a near lake by day only the Pond Perch (100) and the Mud Carp (90) can bite, so the Perch comes up 100 times in 190.

Each fish's weight is rolled within its range, rounded to 0.1 kg. Heavy fish are rarer than light ones: a fish lands in the top half of its range only about 3 times in 10. See the full fish reference for every fish's details.

Odds for the legendaries

In a far lake at dawn or dusk, with a Frontier Rod and Prime Bait, the fish that can bite are the Pond Perch (100), Mud Carp (90), Ironjaw Pike (30) and Frontier Sturgeon (6). That makes the Sturgeon about 1 fish bite in 38. In far crude oil at night it's the Slick Minnow (100), Tarback Catfish (50) and Crude Leviathan (5), so the Leviathan is about 1 bite in 31. Crates and junk come up on top of that.

Moonfin hunting

In a near lake at night with Glow Bait, the Moonfin's 45 becomes 112.5 against the Perch's 100 and the Carp's 90, so about 37% of your fish are Moonfins. Without Glow Bait it's about 19%.

docs.title: Junk and Sunken Crates
docs.text: Every cast first rolls for a Sunken Crate, then for junk, and otherwise it's a fish.

docs.title: Sunken Crate
docs.text:
Band Crate chance per cast Near 2% Mid 4% Far 6%

A crate is heavy dead weight on the line: no runs, but the tension climbs fast. Once landed it breaks open and you get the same loot as a vanilla epic loot crate. Crates landed in the far band also have a 5% chance to hold a Backpack Expansion (see Backpack). Anything that doesn't fit in your inventory drops at your feet. The Fish Journal counts the crates the party has hauled up.

docs.title: Junk
docs.text:
If no crate comes up, 12% of casts snag junk instead of a fish. What you get depends on the water:

Water Junk (amount, share of junk catches) Water Scrap Metal Block 1-3 (42%), Scrap Wood Block 1-4 (42%), Component Kit 1 (12.5%), Circuit Board 1 (4%) Chemical Chemical 1-3 (51%), Scrap Metal Block 1-3 (31%), Component Kit 1 (12%), Circuit Board 1 (6%) Crude oil Crude Oil 1-3 (54.5%), Scrap Metal Block 1-3 (30%), Component Kit 1 (10%), Circuit Board 1 (6%)

Junk is dead weight: no runs and no stamina, so just reel it in and ease off if the line gets tight.

docs.title: Fish Fillets
docs.text:
Fish Fillet: put a fish in your hotbar, select it and hold Create for 1.5 seconds. That one fish becomes its fillets: 1 for the smallest fish, up to 12 for a Crude Leviathan (see the table above). Letting go early cancels. If there isn't room in your inventory for the fillets, nothing happens ("No room for the fillets").

Fillets are used in:

  • Prime Bait at the Workbench (3 fillets + 1 Chili Pepper → 2).
  • Grilled Fish at the Campfire (2 fillets), plus several fish dishes at the Cookbot, such as Fish Chowder. Some dishes, such as Smoked Pike, take a whole fish. See Frontier Kitchen and the recipe list.

docs.title: Fish Journal and party records
docs.text:
Type /fish in chat to open the Fish Journal (see Commands). It shows:

  • A summary: how many of the 12 species the party has found, the total fish caught by the party, and how many Sunken Crates were hauled up.
  • Every species. Fish you haven't caught show as dark silhouettes marked ???, with a hint about where and when to look and what rod and bait they need. Caught fish show how many the party has landed and the record weight, with the name of the player who holds it. Legendaries are named in gold.

The records belong to the whole party and are saved with the world. Chat announces each first catch of a species ("Name caught the party's first Moonfin (0.8 kg)!") and each new record ("New Moonfin record: 1.1 kg by Name (was 0.8 kg)"). Legendary catches are prefixed LEGENDARY!

docs.title: Catch Orders
docs.text:
Catch Orders on the Contract Board ask the party to hand in fish, the same way as a supply run. They pay Frontier Scrip and materials like other contracts, plus bait:

Order tier Asks for (one per order) Bait paid 1 6 Lake Fish (any), 4 Glowgills or 4 Slick Minnows 8 Basic Bait 2 3 Moonfins, 3 Sunscale Trout, 6 Mud Carp or 6 Glowgills 6 Glow Bait 3 1 Ironjaw Pike, 2 Sludge Eels or 2 Tarback Catfish 8 Glow Bait + a Frontier Rod* 4 2 Ironjaw Pike, 1 Three-Eyed Tetra or 2 Tarback Catfish 4 Prime Bait + a Frontier Rod* 5 2 Three-Eyed Tetras, 3 Big Fish (any), 1 Frontier Sturgeon† or 1 Crude Leviathan† 6 Prime Bait + a Frontier Rod*

* Only until someone in the party claims a Frontier Rod. † Only offered once the party has a Frontier Rod.

From tier 3 up, most Catch Orders need big fish, so get a Carbon Rod first. See Contracts for how tiers, Frontier Standing and rewards work.

docs.title: Gyro Stabilizer Parts
docs.text:
A set of parts for building your own self-levelling craft: hover platforms, flying machines, anything that has to stay flat. A spinning Gyro Flywheel in a gimbal gives you a steady reference. Angle Encoders measure how far your craft is tilted against it. Small signal parts shape that number, and Throttle Thrusters push by exactly the amount they're told. None of the parts knows what "level" is or how hard to correct. That comes from how you wire and tune them.

Experimental

The gyro parts are experimental. How they behave, and the numbers on this page, may change in later updates. Test new builds somewhere safe: a badly tuned controller or a heavy gimbal can make a craft swing, flip or fling itself.

At a glance

  • Signal flow: Gyro Flywheel → Angle Encoders → Gain / Rate / Mixer / Flip / Clamp / Set Point → Throttle Thrusters. A Scope graphs any signal.
  • Flywheels come in 1x1 (~50 kg), 3x3 (~110 kg) and 5x5 (~250 kg). They need Inverter power and must hang in a gimbal.
  • Throttle Thruster: a signal of 0-100 is its thrust in percent. Full thrust is 8,000 N, enough to hold up about 800 kg.
  • Signals pass along their own kind of wire, and the whole chain reacts in the same tick.
  • How to get them: four Traveling Trader blueprints (Gyro Flywheels, Signal Parts, Throttle Thruster, Carbon Pipes), then craft at the Craftbot.

docs.title: Getting the parts
docs.text:
All the gyro parts are crafted at the Craftbot, once your party has bought the matching blueprint from the Traveling Trader:
